editorial:
Picture a young boy named Maki breaking free from chains in the dead of night, running across moonlit desert sands while slavers chase him. That is how Zarafa pulls you in. Soon he meets a baby giraffe who is also an orphan, and together with a desert nomad named Hassan, they set off on a long journey to deliver the giraffe as a gift to the King of France. The whole thing feels like a classic adventure story, with hand-drawn animation that looks warm and beautiful on screen. You get sweeping views of deserts, mountains, and open skies.

The animation is the real star here, with its old-school hand-drawn style that feels rare today. The story moves at a steady pace and keeps things exciting without being too scary for kids. On the downside, some parts feel a little slow, and younger viewers might lose focus during longer travel scenes. Still, the bond between Maki and Zarafa is sweet and easy to root for. If you enjoy family adventures with heart, this one is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Maki and Zarafa finally reach France, and the giraffe is presented to King Charles as a royal gift. Maki is heartbroken at the thought of losing his friend, but he is also freed from slavery. The big twist is that the whole adventure is being told by an old man to a group of children, and that storyteller turns out to be Hassan. In the end, Maki stays close to Zarafa, and the two orphans find a sense of home and freedom together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic hand-drawn family adventures.
